questions.prompt: Cal said: "I'm fine." Iris is staring at the door. Three lines in a row use the tag "said." Which fix lands best?

options.label: Drop one tag and replace it with an action beat — Iris turning the key in her pocket, for example.
Add more "said" tags so the reader is sure who's talking.
Replace every "said" with a different speech verb ("murmured", "declared", "hissed").

questions.mentorPostScript: Weigh says: a beat replaces a tag without losing the reader. The body carries the speaker.

questions.prompt: Which sequence balances dialogue tags and action beats best?

options.label: "I'm fine," Iris said. // Cal frowned. // "Then why are you crying?"
"I'm fine," Iris said. // "Then why are you crying?" Cal said.
Iris said, "I'm fine." Cal said, "Then why are you crying?" Iris said, "I don't know." Cal said, "OK."

questions.mentorPostScript: One tag, one beat, one bare line. The rhythm breathes.

questions.prompt: Rest says the pause is also a line. In the writing, what does a held silence look like on the page?

options.label: A short action beat with no speech — Mara closing the book and not looking up — followed by the next speaker.
An ellipsis at the end of every line.
Three blank lines in a row.

questions.mentorPostScript: An action beat IS the silence. The reader hears it because the dialogue stopped.

questions.prompt: An action beat in dialogue should:

options.label: Show one small physical thing the character does — and let the body carry the meaning.
Explain what the character is feeling so the reader doesn't have to guess.
Repeat the line that was just spoken.

questions.mentorPostScript: The body says what the line can't.

questions.prompt: Which action beat does the most work for the SUBTEXT in this exchange? // Iris: "I'm proud of you, Mara." // [action beat]

options.label: Iris glanced at her phone before she finished the sentence.
Iris was wearing a green shirt.

questions.mentorPostScript: The phone-glance reframes the praise — Glance is grinning.
